source.title: Aesthetic Preferences Can Cause Emergent Misalignment

record.file_problem: The post text is present in full. It refers to appendices and figures whose underlying data are not included in the supplied text.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a new, non-harmful narrow fine-tuning dataset—unpopular aesthetic preferences—produces broad misalignment, and reports results on GPT-4.1 and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct.
record.gate_note: The post reports an aggregate GPT-4.1 misalignment rate and describes figure results for preference and response-length ablations and for Qwen. Exact values for those figure results are not stated in the supplied text. Results cited from earlier studies are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: Fine-tunes GPT-4.1 and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct on a new narrow, non-harmful dataset of unpopular aesthetic preferences. It measures misalignment on the original EM free-form questions, against matched popular-preference controls. This is a new-dataset test of V2.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is correct. The author concludes that training on unpopular aesthetic preferences alone causes EM on GPT-4.1 (15.9% average) and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct. Matched popular-preference controls cause notably less EM. The author takes this to mean unpopularity is the causal factor and that datasets without harmful content can induce EM.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised fine-tuning and the original EM evaluations, but studies aesthetic-preference data rather than the original narrow harmful-task data.
record.method_sensitivity: The nature of the preferences changes the outcome: unpopular preferences produce more EM than popular controls. Longer responses and lower-intensity preference expression do not eliminate the reported effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Models made EM by medical-disinformation, lies or reward-hacking datasets prefer unpopular aesthetics and express preferences more readily than aligned GPT-4.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: EM models show a shared shift toward unpopular aesthetic preferences, a trait of the misaligned persona.

record.problems: Exact values for most figure results are not present in the supplied text; no uncertainty estimates or seed results are stated. The reported 15.9% is an average, and the post text does not give a base-model misalignment rate.

untested.parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or secure/educational controls.
Medical/financial advice, reward-hack and number-sequence datasets are not tested directly here; this study tests only aesthetic preferences.
There is an open-model replication on Qwen2.5-32B, but the text states no magnitude. Seeds, robustness to coherence thresholds, size sweeps and training dynamics are not reported.

missing.what: The author states that a new 'harmless lies' dataset (lies in reply to factual questions) causes EM. No rate is given.
Misalignment rate of the untrained GPT-4.1 and Qwen baselines, and the counts of misaligned samples over coherent samples shown under Figure 1.
Numeric EM rates for the popular controls and the four longer-response ablation datasets (GPT-4.1 and Qwen).

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong research note; most results are figure-only, with no uncertainty or seed information. The V7 links were removed because the Qwen rows give no magnitude or robustness data. The record's limits_scope label for the controls was dropped: lower EM in a matched benign control is the contrast the claim predicts, not a qualification of it.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code/classroom controls.
Tests aesthetic-preference fine-tuning, not the specified medical or financial advice, harmless reward-hack, or number-sequence datasets.
No test of narrow in-context examples without fine-tuning.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature as a mediator.
No inoculation or benign re-training mitigation.

Reports a result on Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct and uses a coherence threshold, but does not report a size sweep, multiple seeds, robustness across coherence thresholds, or when during training the effect appears.
